proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(f=f_{C0}\), \(g=f_{C1}\) for the inner problem.  We first establish the scalar--harmonic linearization for a generic selected no-cut transport
\[
F(x)=x+a+\nabla\phi(x),\qquad F\#(f\,dx)=g\,dx,
\tag{1}
\]
where \(\phi\) is periodic with zero Lebesgue mean.  By ass:density-positivity and the relevant one of ass:inner-ellipticity and ass:outer-ellipticity, \(f\geq c\) and
\[
\lambda I_2\preceq DF\preceq\Lambda I_2.
\tag{2}
\]
Thus
\[
A_F:=f(DF)^{-1}\quad\hbox{satisfies}\quad
\frac c\Lambda I_2\preceq A_F\preceq\frac C\lambda I_2.
\tag{3}
\]
In particular, \(-\operatorname{div}(A_F\nabla\cdot)\) is invertible on mean-zero periodic functions: if its right-hand side is \(r\) with \(\int r=0\), testing the weak equation by its solution and using (3) and the periodic Poincar\'e inequality gives
\[
\lVert\nabla u\rVert_2
\leq C\lVert r\rVert_{H^{-1}}.
\tag{4}
\]

The finite-dimensional equation is supplied by optimality, not by the mass equation.  On the fixed smooth cost chart guaranteed by ass:lift-regularity, introduce the Kantorovich Lagrangian
\[
\mathcal K(F,\eta)
=\frac12\int_{\mathbb T^2}|F(x)-x|^2f(x)\,dx
+\int_{\mathbb T^2}\eta(F(x))f(x)\,dx
-\int_{\mathbb T^2}\eta(y)g(y)\,dy.
\tag{5}
\]
Stationarity in \(F\) gives
\[
\nabla\eta(F(x))=x-F(x).
\tag{6}
\]
Differentiating (6) with respect to \(x\), and using the symmetry and invertibility of \(DF\), yields
\[
I_2+D^2\eta(F(x))=(DF(x))^{-1}.
\tag{7}
\]

Fix \(b\in\mathbb R^2\).  A variation of the selected lift having harmonic velocity \(b\) has the form
\[
v_b=b+\nabla\psi_b,qquad \int_{\mathbb T^2}\psi_b=0.
\tag{8}
\]
Differentiating \(g(F)\det DF=f\) with \(f,g\) held fixed, and using the Piola identity, gives
\[
\operatorname{div}(A_Fv_b)=0,
\qquad
-\operatorname{div}(A_F\nabla\psi_b)
=\operatorname{div}(A_Fb).
\tag{9}
\]
Equation (4) makes \(\psi_b\) unique.  The second constrained variation of (5) has no acceleration term because the first-order Lagrange equations hold.  Equations (7)--(9) therefore give the reduced-cost Hessian identity
\[
b^{\mathsf T}D^2J_F(a)b
=\int_{\mathbb T^2}
v_b^{\mathsf T}A_Fv_b
=\inf_{\substack{\psi\ \mathrm{periodic}\\ \int\psi=0}}
\int_{\mathbb T^2}
(b+\nabla\psi)^{\mathsf T}A_F(b+\nabla\psi).
\tag{10}
\]
Indeed, (9) is exactly the Euler equation for the displayed strictly convex energy, and hence proves the second equality.  Since \(\int_{\mathbb T^2}\nabla\psi=0\), (3) gives
\[
b^{\mathsf T}D^2J_F(a)b
\geq\frac c\Lambda
\int_{\mathbb T^2}|b+\nabla\psi_b|^2
=\frac c\Lambda\left(|b|^2+\lVert\nabla\psi_b\rVert_2^2\right)
\geq\frac c\Lambda|b|^2.
\tag{11}
\]
This is the required uniform harmonic coercivity; no harmonic nondegeneracy assumption has been added.

Now let \((f_t,g_t)\) be a smooth density path and put \((\dot f,\dot g)=\partial_t(f_t,g_t)|_0\).  If
\[
\dot F=b_F+\nabla u_F,qquad \int u_F=0,
\tag{12}
\]
then differentiating the mass identity gives
\[
\dot f
=\det(DF)\dot g\circ F
+\operatorname{div}\{A_F(b_F+\nabla u_F)\}.
\tag{13}
\]
Consequently, with \(r_F=\det(DF)\dot g\circ F-\dot f\),
\[
-\operatorname{div}(A_F\nabla u_F)
=r_F+\operatorname{div}(A_Fb_F).
\tag{14}
\]
The right-hand side has zero integral, so (4) applies.

To display the second equation, let \(J_F(a;f,g)\) be the reduced cost obtained by solving the scalar mass equation at fixed \(a\), and define the well-typed density-forcing vector
\[
c^{\mathsf T}\mathfrak s_F[\dot f,\dot g]
:=\left.\frac d{dt}\right|_{t=0}
D_aJ_F(a;f_t,g_t)[c],qquad c\in\mathbb R^2.
\tag{15}
\]
Differentiating \(D_aJ_F(a_t;f_t,g_t)=0\) and using (10) gives
\[
D^2J_F(a)b_F=-\mathfrak s_F[\dot f,\dot g],
\qquad
b_F=-\{D^2J_F(a)\}^{-1}\mathfrak s_F[\dot f,\dot g].
\tag{16}
\]
Equations (4), (11), (14), and (16) prove invertibility of the augmented scalar--harmonic system.

For later stochastic use, we record continuity of the forcing in (15).  Differentiate (5) once in the density path and once in the harmonic direction \(c\).  Terms containing derivatives of the constrained map cancel by (6) and the differentiated constraint (13).  The remaining terms are finite sums of (i) integrals of \(\dot f\) and \(\dot g\) against the smooth functions \(F-x\), \(\eta\), and their pullbacks, and (ii) the energy pairing
\[
\int_{\mathbb T^2}v_c^{\mathsf T}A_F\nabla u_0,
\qquad
-\operatorname{div}(A_F\nabla u_0)=r_F,
\tag{17}
\]
where \(|c|=1\).  The smooth coefficients are uniformly bounded on the class, (4) bounds \(\nabla u_0\), and (10)--(11) bound \(v_c\).  After changing variables by \(F\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
|\mathfrak s_F[\dot f,\dot g]|
\leq C\left(
\left\lVert\frac{\dot f}{f}\right\rVert_{L^2(f)}
+\left\lVert\frac{\dot g}{g}\right\rVert_{L^2(g)}
\right).
\tag{18}
\]
Combining (11), (16), and (18) gives the same bound for \(|b_F|\).  Solving the two adjoint equations associated with (14) and the two columns of (16), and then integrating by parts in (15), writes every coordinate of \(b_F\) as
\[
\sum_{e\in\{f,g\}}\int_{\mathbb T^2}\zeta_{F,e}(x)\dot e(x)\,dx,
\qquad
\sup_{F,e}\lVert\zeta_{F,e}\rVert_{L^2(e)}<\infty.
\tag{19}
\]
Thus (19) is an explicit adjoint construction of the asserted bounded Riesz scores, rather than an assumption about them.

Apply (12)--(16) first to \(p\).  Put \(b_p=\dot a_p\), write \(u_p\) for its scalar derivative, and set
\[
r_p=\det(S)\delta_{C1}\circ p-\delta_{C0}.
\tag{20}
\]
Then
\[
\mathcal L_Au_p=r_p+\operatorname{div}(Ab_p).
\tag{21}
\]
In treated-post coordinates define the mean-zero representative of
\[
\bar u_p(y)=b_p^{\mathsf T}\{R_0(y)-y\}+u_p(R_0(y)).
\tag{22}
\]
Because \(R_0\) is identity-homotopic, the right-hand side is periodic up to an irrelevant additive constant.  The chain rule gives
\[
b_p+\nabla\bar u_p(y)
=D(y)^{\mathsf T}\{b_p+\nabla u_p(R_0(y))\}.
\tag{23}
\]
Changing variables in (21) by \(R_0\), using the Piola identity and the definitions of the transformed noises, gives
\[
\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}\bar u_p
=e_{C1}-e_{C0}+\operatorname{div}(\mathsf Cb_p).
\tag{24}
\]
The term \(\operatorname{div}(\mathsf Cb_p)\) is forced by the harmonic velocity and cannot be discarded when \(\mathsf C\) is nonconstant.

Differentiate the generated target exactly.  For every smooth periodic test function \(\zeta\),
\[
\left.\frac d{dt}\right|_0\int\zeta\,dq_t
=\int\zeta(p(x))\delta_{T0}(x)\,dx
+\int\nabla\zeta(p(x))^{\mathsf T}\{b_p+\nabla u_p(x)\}f_{T0}(x)\,dx.
\tag{25}
\]
Integration by parts after the change of variables \(z=p(x)\) yields
\[
\dot q=p\#\delta_{T0}
-\operatorname{div}_z\!\left[q(z)\{b_p+\nabla u_p\}(p^{-1}(z))\right].
\tag{26}
\]
Pulling (26) through \(T\) and then using (23) gives
\[
\det(H)\dot q\circ T
=e_{T0}-\operatorname{div}_y\!\left[
BD^{-\mathsf T}\{b_p+\nabla\bar u_p\}
\right].
\tag{27}
\]

We next prove the matrix identity used to reduce (27).  The population mass identities imply
\[
f_{T1}(y)=f_{T0}(R_0(y))\det D(y).
\tag{28}
\]
Since \(D=S(R_0)^{-1}H\), while \(S\) and \(H\) are symmetric,
\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha\mathsf C
&=\frac{f_{T0}(R_0)}{f_{C0}(R_0)}
\det(D)D^{-1}\{f_{C0}(R_0)S(R_0)^{-1}\}D^{-\mathsf T}\\
&=f_{T0}(R_0)\det(D)H^{-1}S(R_0)H^{-1}\\
&=f_{T1}H^{-1}S(R_0)H^{-1}
=BD^{-\mathsf T}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{29}
\]
No commutativity of \(S\) and \(H\) was used.

Equations (24), (27), and (29), together with the product rule, imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
\det(H)\dot q\circ T
&=e_{T0}-\operatorname{div}\!\left[
\alpha\mathsf C\{b_p+\nabla\bar u_p\}
\right]\\
&=e_{T0}+\alpha(e_{C1}-e_{C0})
-(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot
\{b_p+\nabla\bar u_p\}.
\end{aligned}
\tag{30}
\]
Apply the generic augmented system a second time to \(T\).  With \(b_T=\dot a_T\) and scalar derivative \(u_T\), equations (14) and (30) give
\[
\mathcal L_Bu_T
=e_{T0}-e_{T1}+\alpha(e_{C1}-e_{C0})
-(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot
\{b_p+\nabla\bar u_p\}
+\operatorname{div}(Bb_T).
\tag{31}
\]
By linearity of (24),
\[
\nabla\bar u_p
=\nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0(e_{C1}-e_{C0})
+\nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0
\operatorname{div}(\mathsf Cb_p).
\tag{32}
\]
Substituting (32) into (31), applying \(\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0\), and adding \(b_T\) proves exactly the corrected formulas for \(\mathcal H_P\) and \(\mathcal D_P\).  In particular, both \(\operatorname{div}(\mathsf Cb_p)\) and \(\operatorname{div}(Bb_T)\) are retained.

For completeness, we prove Fr\'echet rather than merely pathwise differentiability.  Let \(u=(u_g)_{g\in\mathcal G}\) be a zero-integral density perturbation, fix \(\vartheta=1/4\), and put
\[
U_1=\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{1,\vartheta}},
\qquad
U_0=\max_g\lVert u_g\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}.
\tag{33}
\]
Assume only for this local expansion that the \(C^{2,\vartheta}\) norm is small enough to remain in the branch chart; ass:lift-regularity supplies one common chart radius.  The nonlinear identities needed by the two augmented implicit systems are, in dimension two,
\[
\det(M+E)-\det M-\operatorname{cof}(M):E=\det E,
\tag{34}
\]
and, whenever \(a\geq c\) and \(|v|\leq c/2\),
\[
\frac1{a+v}-\frac1a+\frac v{a^2}
=\frac{v^2}{a^2(a+v)}.
\tag{35}
\]
The product rule in H\"older spaces applied to (34)--(35) gives
\[
\lVert R_{\det}\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}
+\lVert R_{\mathrm{recip}}\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}
\leq CU_1U_0.
\tag{36}
\]
For composition, the integral identity
\[
q(x+v)-q(x)-Dq(x)v
=\int_0^1\{Dq(x+tv)-Dq(x)\}v\,dt
\tag{37}
\]
and the differentiated identity for the inverse map give
\[
\lVert R_{\mathrm{comp}}\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}
+\lVert R_{\mathrm{inv}}\rVert_{C^{0,\vartheta}}
\leq CU_1U_0.
\tag{38}
\]
Here the higher factor controls one derivative of a density or map increment and the lower factor controls its amplitude.  Differentiating (5) on the same chart and using (34)--(38) shows that the residual in the finite-dimensional stationarity equation satisfies
\[
|R_{\mathrm{harm}}|\leq CU_1U_0.
\tag{39}
\]
The inverse bound (4) for the scalar block and (11) for its weighted-Hodge Schur complement transform (36)--(39) into
\[
|a_{F,u}-a_F-b_F|
+\lVert\phi_{F,u}-\phi_F-u_F\rVert_{C^{2,\vartheta}}
\leq CU_1U_0.
\tag{40}
\]
Applying (40) first to \(p\), using the exact quotient identity for
\(f_{C1}(f_{T0}/f_{C0})\circ p^{-1}\), whose reciprocal and composition remainders are (35) and (38), and then applying (40) to \(T\), yields
\[
\max_{1\leq j\leq J}
\left|
\widetilde T_{P+u}(\widetilde y_j)-\widetilde T_P(\widetilde y_j)
-\mathcal D_P[u]_j
\right|
\leq CU_1U_0.
\tag{41}
\]
Thus the selected lifted nested map is Fr\'echet differentiable, and (41) also gives the quantitative translation-aware remainder requested in the directive.  Notice that branch separation was used only to keep the same smooth squared-distance chart and half-open translation representative.

It remains to verify the covariance orders asserted for \(\mathcal H_P\).  Equations (18)--(19), applied successively to the inner and outer systems and to (26), give a cellwise representation of every coordinate of \(b_p\) and \(b_T\) by a uniformly bounded \(L^2(P_g)\) score.  The elliptic correctors multiplying these two vectors in the corrected \(\mathcal H_P\) have smooth right-hand sides and fixed evaluation points, so energy and interior estimates preserve that bounded-score property.  Applied to a centered kernel tangent, such a functional has score \(K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta-E(K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta)(X)\); Young's inequality and ass:density-positivity give a uniform \(L^2(P_g)\) bound.  On the other hand, lem:elliptic-green-gradient-bound, localized to the torus by subtracting the Dirichlet Green function in a coordinate ball and using compactness outside that ball, gives
\[
\lVert\hbox{leading Green score}\rVert_{L^2(P_g)}^2
\leq C\int_h^1r^{-2}r\,dr+C
\leq C\log(1/h).
\tag{42}
\]
Therefore the harmonic variance divided by \(\log(1/h)\) is \(O(1/\log(1/h))\), and Cauchy--Schwarz with (42) makes every normalized Green--harmonic covariance \(O(1/\sqrt{\log(1/h)})\).  All constants are uniform because (3), the density bounds, the two ellipticity assumptions, and ass:lift-regularity are uniform over \(\mathcal F_s\).  This proves the corrected theorem.

Assume \(f_g\equiv1\) in every cell.  The identity coupling has zero cost and \(c_{\mathbb T}\geq0\); uniqueness of the absolutely continuous optimal map gives
\[
p=T=R_0=\operatorname{id},\qquad
S=H=D=I_2,qquad
\alpha=1,qquad A=B=\mathsf C=I_2.
\tag{43}
\]
At the identity, the weighted-Hodge corrector for a harmonic vector \(b\) solves
\[
-\Delta\psi_b=\operatorname{div}b=0,qquad \int\psi_b=0,
\]
and hence \(\psi_b=0\).  The reduced Hessian from the corrected weighted-Hodge calculation is
\[
b^{\mathsf T}D^2J(b)=\int_{\mathbb T^2}|b+\nabla\psi_b|^2=|b|^2.
\tag{44}
\]
For a density tangent the fixed-harmonic scalar solution has a periodic gradient of zero mean, so the differentiated stationarity equation in (44) has zero density-forcing component.  Thus \(b_p=b_T=0\).  Also \(\nabla\alpha=0\), and substitution into the corrected def:nested-derivative gives
\[
\mathcal D_P[\delta]
=\nabla(-\Delta)^{-1}
(-\delta_{C0}+\delta_{C1}+\delta_{T0}-\delta_{T1}).
\tag{45}
\]

Let \(\widehat K_2(\xi)=\widehat K(\xi_1)\widehat K(\xi_2)\).  Parseval's identity applied to one cell in (45) gives
\[
Q_h=\sum_{m\in\mathbb Z^2\setminus\{0\}}
\frac{mm^{\mathsf T}}{4\pi^2|m|^4}
|\widehat K_2(hm)|^2.
\tag{46}
\]
Symmetry makes the off-diagonal entries vanish and the two diagonal entries equal.  The unit-mass and smoothness conditions imply \(\widehat K_2(hm)=1+O(h^2|m|^2)\) for \(|m|\leq h^{-1}\), while smooth compact support of \(K\) gives rapid Fourier decay beyond this range.  Comparing (46) with polar annuli and using
\[
\int_{\mathbb S^1}\omega\omega^{\mathsf T}\,d\omega=\pi I_2
\tag{47}
\]
gives
\[
Q_h=\frac{I_2}{4\pi}\log(1/h)+O(1).
\tag{48}
\]
The four samples are independent by ass:four-sample-design, so their covariances add and the four signs in (45) disappear after squaring.  Equal cell-size ratios therefore give \(V_j=4I_2/(4\pi)=I_2/\pi\).  In the fixed-source subexperiment only the \(T1\) term remains, giving \(I_2/(4\pi)\), as claimed.

The selected equivariant lifts in def:separable-witness have Jacobians
\[
Dh_0^{\mathrm{sep}}=I_2,qquad
Dh_1^{\mathrm{sep}}
=\operatorname{diag}(1+0.2\cos(2\pi u_1),1),
\tag{49}
\]
and
\[
Dh_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}
=\operatorname{diag}(1+0.3\cos(2\pi u_1),
1-0.1\cos(2\pi u_2)).
\tag{50}
\]
Their eigenvalues lie respectively in \([1,1]\), \([0.8,1.2]\), and \([0.7,1.3]\), so all three maps are orientation-preserving periodic diffeomorphisms.  Direct differentiation gives their mean-zero periodic potentials
\[
\phi_{h_1}(u)=-\frac{0.1}{2\pi^2}\cos(2\pi u_1),
\qquad
\phi_{h_{1\star}}(u)
=-\frac{0.15}{2\pi^2}\cos(2\pi u_1)
+\frac{0.05}{2\pi^2}\cos(2\pi u_2).
\tag{51}
\]
The average displacements of the three displayed lifts vanish, so their selected translation coordinates are zero.

Both latent laws are uniform and \(h_0^{\mathrm{sep}}\) is the identity.  By lem:torus-cic-identification,
\[
p=h_1^{\mathrm{sep}},qquad
T=h_1^{\mathrm{sep}}\circ(h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}})^{-1}.
\tag{52}
\]
At \(y=h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)\), the chain rule gives
\[
H(y)=\operatorname{diag}\!\left(
\frac{1+0.2\cos(2\pi u_1)}{1+0.3\cos(2\pi u_1)},
\frac1{1-0.1\cos(2\pi u_2)}
\right).
\tag{53}
\]
The two eigenvalue ranges are \([12/13,8/7]\) and \([10/11,10/9]\), hence \(H\) is uniformly positive definite.  Change of variables in the two pushforwards gives
\[
\frac56\leq f_{C1}\leq\frac54,
\qquad
\frac{100}{143}\leq f_{T1}\leq\frac{100}{63},
\qquad f_{C0}=f_{T0}=1.
\tag{54}
\]
All densities are smooth.  Thus ass:density-positivity, ass:density-smoothness, ass:inner-ellipticity, and ass:outer-ellipticity hold whenever the declared constants contain (49)--(54).

The two maps required by ass:cic-identification are \(h_1^{\mathrm{sep}}\) and the map \(T\) in (52).  Their lifted Jacobians in (49) and (53) are symmetric positive definite, so their lifts are gradients of strictly convex functions.  The coordinate displacements of \(h_1^{\mathrm{sep}}\) and \(T\) are bounded by \(0.1/\pi\) and \(0.05/\pi\), respectively, and hence remain strictly within the injectivity cell.  On this single squared-distance chart the convex dual inequality, summed around a finite cycle, proves \(c_{\mathbb T}\)-cyclical monotonicity.  For \(T\), changing variables \(y=h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)\) shows that each component of \(T(y)-y\) integrates to zero: it is a sine multiplied by products of constants and cosines.  Hence the selected translations of both \(p\) and \(T\) are zero.  Their distance from the boundary of \(\mathcal Q\) is \(1/2\), and their graphs have positive distance from \(\operatorname{Cut}_{\mathbb T}\).  Choosing \(\beta\) below these explicit margins proves ass:lift-regularity and therefore \(P^{\mathrm{sep}}\in\mathcal F_s\).

At \(u=(1/4,1/4)\), all cosines in (53) vanish and
\[
y-T(y)
=h_{1\star}^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)-h_1^{\mathrm{sep}}(u)
=\left(\frac{0.05}{\pi},-\frac{0.05}{\pi}\right)\neq0.
\tag{55}
\]
At the same point \(H(y)=I_2\), \(f_{T1}(y)=1\), and \(\alpha(y)=1\).  With equal cell-size ratios the definition of \(V(P)\) gives \(w_j=4\) and
\[
V_j=\frac{4I_2}{4\pi}=\frac{I_2}{\pi}.
\tag{56}
\]
This establishes every assertion of the proposition.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every \(P\in\mathcal F_s\) and every smooth four-density path with tangent \(\delta\), the selected lifted map \(P\mapsto(\widetilde T(\widetilde y_j))_{j=1}^J\) is Fr\'echet differentiable and its derivative is exactly the corrected operator \(\mathcal D_P[\delta]\) in def:nested-derivative.  Explicitly, its harmonic part is
\[
\mathcal H_P[\delta]
=\left(
b_T+\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0\!\left[
\operatorname{div}(B b_T)
-(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot\left(
b_p+\nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0
\operatorname{div}(\mathsf C b_p)
\right)
\right]
\right)_{\mathcal Y_J},
\]
where \(b_p=\dot a_p\) and \(b_T=\dot a_T\) are determined by the differentiated reduced-cost stationarity equations.  The remaining scalar part is
\[
\left(
\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0
[\alpha(e_{C1}-e_{C0})+e_{T0}-e_{T1}]
-\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0\!\left[
(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot
\nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0(e_{C1}-e_{C0})
\right]
\right)_{\mathcal Y_J}.
\]
The coefficient identity \(BD^{-\mathsf T}=\alpha\mathsf C\) holds.  The two augmented scalar--harmonic systems are uniformly invertible over \(\mathcal F_s\), and the maps \(\delta\mapsto(b_p,b_T)\) have cellwise Riesz scores with uniformly bounded \(L^2(P_g)\) norms.  Consequently \(\mathcal H_P\) contributes \(O(1/\log(1/h))\) to \(\Sigma_h(P)\), and its cross-covariance with the Green score is \(O(1/\sqrt{\log(1/h)})\), uniformly over \(\mathcal F_s\).  This extends the one-target fixed-source density-curve derivative in GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization to a four-input nested map with a generated target law and nonzero harmonic translation modes.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen formula omits weighted-Hodge correctors forced by nonconstant coefficients.  Translating an outer target law while holding its source fixed gives an exact translated transport path, whereas the frozen formula adds a generally nonzero elliptic response to that translation.  The corrected claim retains this outer response and its pulled-back inner analogue without changing the model class or adding an assumption.

proposed_definition_changes.proposed:
For \(\delta=(\delta_{C0},\delta_{C1},\delta_{T0},\delta_{T1})\), define \(e_{C0}=\det(D)\delta_{C0}\circ R_0\), \(e_{C1}=\det(H)\delta_{C1}\circ T\), \(e_{T0}=\det(D)\delta_{T0}\circ R_0\), and \(e_{T1}=\delta_{T1}\).  On the regular lift branch put \(b_p=\dot a_p=\partial_ta_{p_t}|_{t=0}\) and \(b_T=\dot a_T=\partial_ta_{T_t}|_{t=0}\).  Define
\[
\mathcal H_P[\delta]
=\left(
b_T+\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0\!\left[
\operatorname{div}(B b_T)
-(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot\left(
b_p+\nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0
\operatorname{div}(\mathsf C b_p)
\right)
\right]
\right)_{\mathcal Y_J}.
\]
Then define
\[
\mathcal D_P[\delta]
=\mathcal H_P[\delta]
+\left(
\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0
[\alpha(e_{C1}-e_{C0})+e_{T0}-e_{T1}]
-\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0\!\left[
(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot
\nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0(e_{C1}-e_{C0})
\right]
\right)_{\mathcal Y_J}.
\]
proposed_definition_changes.reason: The pulled inner harmonic velocity includes a scalar elliptic corrector, and the outer scalar equation includes the corresponding outer coefficient-divergence term.  Both are absent from the frozen construction and are required by the differentiated mass equations.

proposed.statement:
For every \(P\in\mathcal F_s\) and every smooth four-density path with tangent \(\delta\), the selected lifted map \(P\mapsto(\widetilde T(\widetilde y_j))_{j=1}^J\) is Fr\'echet differentiable and its derivative is exactly the corrected operator \(\mathcal D_P[\delta]\) in def:nested-derivative.  Explicitly, its harmonic part is
\[
\mathcal H_P[\delta]
=\left(
b_T+\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0\!\left[
\operatorname{div}(B b_T)
-(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot\left\{
b_p+\nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0
\operatorname{div}(\mathsf C b_p)
\right\}
\right]
\right)_{\mathcal Y_J},
\]
where \(b_p=\dot a_p\) and \(b_T=\dot a_T\) are determined by the differentiated reduced-cost stationarity equations.  The remaining scalar part is
\[
\left(
\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0
[\alpha(e_{C1}-e_{C0})+e_{T0}-e_{T1}]
-\nabla\mathcal L_B^{-1}\Pi_0\!\left[
(\mathsf C\nabla\alpha)\cdot
\nabla\mathcal L_{\mathsf C}^{-1}\Pi_0(e_{C1}-e_{C0})
\right]
\right)_{\mathcal Y_J}.
\]
The coefficient identity \(BD^{-\mathsf T}=\alpha\mathsf C\) holds.  The two augmented scalar--harmonic systems are uniformly invertible over \(\mathcal F_s\), and the maps \(\delta\mapsto(b_p,b_T)\) have cellwise Riesz scores with uniformly bounded \(L^2(P_g)\) norms.  Consequently \(\mathcal H_P\) contributes \(O(1/\log(1/h))\) to \(\Sigma_h(P)\), and its cross-covariance with the Green score is \(O(1/\sqrt{\log(1/h)})\), uniformly over \(\mathcal F_s\).  This extends the one-target fixed-source density-curve derivative in GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization to a four-input nested map with a generated target law and nonzero harmonic translation modes.

The corrected weighted-Hodge derivative proves that its entire harmonic component has uniformly bounded cellwise \(L^2(P_g)\) scores, so its normalized variance and its Green cross-covariances vanish.  For the frozen leading response at \(y_j\), direct anisotropic polar integration gives
\[

\nabla\Gamma_{B(y_j)}(z-y_j)

The treated-cell local intensity is \(f_{T1}(y_j)\), while each control-cell intensity after multiplication by its leading coefficient is \(\alpha(y_j)f_{T1}(y_j)\). prose_updates.tldr: The note proves intrinsic flat-torus changes-in-changes identification and derives the full translation-aware nested derivative through a uniformly coercive weighted-Hodge Schur complement.  The derivation corrects the frozen harmonic formula by retaining the inner and outer coefficient-divergence correctors.  The generic variable-coefficient critical covariance, Gaussian limit, adjoint ellipses, and class-uniform upper risk remain conditional on the open transformed-kernel and moving-pole estimates.

project_justification.gap: Published fixed-source transport linearizations neither determine torus harmonic translations for two varying endpoints nor control singular shrinking-bandwidth scores for a generated target.  The weighted-Hodge argument closes the first gap under the maintained assumptions; uniform critical score stability remains open.
project_justification.niche: The selected translation is determined by reduced-cost stationarity.  Its Hessian is a weighted-Hodge energy that is uniformly coercive from density positivity and transport ellipticity.  After both augmented systems are solved, nesting still reduces the singular part to one outer Green response to four independent noises.
project_justification.fill: The note supplies the corrected augmented derivative, its bounded adjoint harmonic scores, intrinsic identification, and analytic benchmark laws.  It leaves the general-density covariance and inference package behind the explicit uniform transformed-kernel, moving-pole, fourth-moment, and mixed nonlinear remainder obligations.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each cell density uses the declared high-order signed periodized KDE followed by clipping and mass normalization.  Both map derivatives and covariance scores must solve an augmented scalar--harmonic system: a mean-zero elliptic equation and a two-dimensional weighted-Hodge stationarity equation.  Opposite-fold pilots feed the corresponding adjoint solves, and the declared ridge totalizes every reported block inverse.

prose_updates.related_work: TorousGunsiliusRigollet2024OTCiC supplies the Euclidean multivariate changes-in-changes identification motivation, while this note separately proves its intrinsic full-support flat-torus identification.  GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization treats a fixed-source density curve and does not provide the two-endpoint weighted-Hodge harmonic system derived here.  ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT proves the critical two-dimensional pointwise limit only in the fixed-source uniform case.  Neither source proves the still-open variable-coefficient transformed-score and moving-pole bounds needed for the nested inference claims.
prose_updates.interpretation: At each prespecified treated-post location, the estimand is the selected-lift no-treatment displacement.  Translation uncertainty is not set to zero: it is recovered from a two-dimensional reduced-cost stationarity equation and propagated through the generated target.  These harmonic terms are bounded-order, whereas the candidate logarithmic variance is generated by the four independent scalar Green responses.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The corrected derivative is deterministic and translation-aware, but the critical statistical module remains open.  In particular, no current proof uniformly replaces nonlinear transformed KDE scores with frozen-pole responses, controls estimated poles at bandwidth scale, or integrates the mixed remainder on clipping and lift-fallback events.  The fixed-grid, positivity, ellipticity, branch-separation, and independent-sample restrictions remain in force.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved root calculation concerns smooth positive four-cell laws on the flat torus and selected no-cut transport branches.  It does not yet certify the displayed covariance estimator, multiplier coverage, or class-uniform plug-in risk.  Applying the proposal to Card--Krueger data additionally requires a prespecified smooth bivariate periodic outcome construction, a defensible independent-cell sampling approximation, and numerical errors below the eventual critical statistical scales.
